taste.name: Ink-only restraint
taste.trigger: When facing a product whose entire output is color (palettes, logos, brand boards)
taste.decision: Chose fully monochrome app chrome over any branded accent color
taste.reason: A visible product-brand accent color would visually compete with the user's own brand being built on screen
evidence: #FD7947 scoped to error states only, never a primary action

taste.name: Thread persistence over wizard
taste.trigger: When designing a 12-step conversational form where an early answer can invalidate later ones
taste.decision: Chose to keep every answered step permanently visible and re-editable over a single-screen Back/Next wizard
taste.reason: Showing the dependency chain honestly is more trustworthy than a Back button that hides what re-answering actually invalidates
evidence: all steps render simultaneously across every captured state
zero centered layout moments; no step-counter/progress affordance observed

taste.name: One pill shape for every choice-type
taste.trigger: When the flow needed both single-select (category, visual mode) and multi-select (avoid list, name styles) controls
taste.decision: Chose one identical chip visual for both interaction types over giving multi-select its own affordance
taste.reason: One learned tap-to-toggle pattern scans faster across a long form than stopping to parse each row's selection rule
evidence: 99px radius is the most-used radius in the system, 61 occurrences
no visual differentiator between single- and multi-select chips

taste.name: Inset hairlines over shadow
taste.trigger: When needing to separate cards/inputs from the canvas behind them
taste.decision: Chose a 1px inset border as the default depth cue, reserving real shadow for exactly two states (panel lift, active pick)
taste.reason: Using shadow everywhere would cheapen the two moments where elevation is actually meaningful
evidence: 84 of 91 sampled shadow values are inset hairlines
genuine offset/blur shadow appears only 6 times total
